newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico details record 1996-1997 sugar crop.
newsitem.headline: Mexico details record 1996-1997 sugar crop.

text.p: Mexico's preliminary 1996-1997 sugar crop output reached a record 4.544 million tonnes, compared with 4.378 million tonnes in the 1995-1996 harvest, the National Sugar Chamber said on Wednesday.
The final preliminary figures show 1996-1997 season sugar output jumped 3.8 percent from the previous crop.
The crop output figures were slightly above initial preliminary numbers reported to Reuters last week.
Mexico has seen record sugar harvests for the past four crops. "It is due to increased productivity at the mills, because installed capacity has remained the same," the chamber said in a statement.
The harvest lasted from Oct. 26 to July 19, as mills ran into July instead of ending as normal in June.
It said exports would be about 600,000 tonnes from the crop, or what was left over from national consumption of approximately 3.9 million tonnes per year.

National sugar demand has been hurt by suffering purchasing power and the demand for high fructose corn syrup, principally in the soft drink industry. Mexico recently slapped stiff anti-dumping tariffs on high fructose corn syrup imports.
